title: Precision of antimatter free-fall tests
bottleneck: The ALPHA-g experiment at CERN has shown that antihydrogen falls downward in Earth's gravity, ruling out antigravity models in which antimatter would fall up. But the measurement precision remains around the tens-of-percent level, far from testing whether antimatter falls at exactly the same rate as ordinary matter as the weak equivalence principle demands.
why_it_blocks: A difference in gravitational acceleration between matter and antimatter would overturn general relativity's founding assumption and open a window on quantum gravity. Precision free-fall tests are one of the few direct experimental handles on how gravity treats antimatter.
current_state: ALPHA-g continues to accumulate statistics toward percent-level precision, while competing approaches using positronium, muonium, and charged-particle traps are in development. Reaching the precision of matter-based equivalence-principle tests, parts per 10^15, remains a distant goal.
